newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: WMC says on track for production cost cut.
newsitem.headline: WMC says on track for production cost cut.

text.p: Resources group WMC Ltd said it had begun the 1997/98 financial year well within its target to cut production costs by more than 10 percent.
"For the coming year we are committed to achieving well in excess of a ten percent reduction," managing director Hugh Morgan told a business briefing here on Tuesday night.
"And as we see the costs of production in the first month we are well on track to achieving that, in excess of that," he said.

"We are still working through our cost of sales, some of the stock that was accumulated at the higher cost...but we are heading in the right direction," he told the Securities Institute of Australia dinner briefing.

Morgan also said that two major contracts - for a phosphuric acid plant and a granulation plant - were due to be let in the next month for the company's A$750 million fertiliser project at Phosphate Hill in Queensland.
These would be worth "hundreds of millions (of dollars) each," he later told reporters. WMC, which is based in Melbourne, is a world-ranked miner of uranium, nickel and gold.
Speaking to reporters, Morgan refused to comment on his involvement with the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) during its recent deliberations on selling 167 tonnes of gold.
"I am bound by secrecy...I will say nothing about the Reserve Bank, period," he said. Morgan is a member of the RBA board, which meets each month.
